findings.summary: T058 and T059 deviate from their task descriptions. T058 (missing Code Unit) tests that the runner THROWS instead of transitioning to Failed with TerminalReasonKind.MissingCodeUnit; the MissingCodeUnit reason kind is never asserted in any test. T059 (oversized packet) documents that OverLimitPacket is structurally unreachable via the public CodeUnit API (CodeUnit enforces SymbolName<=512 and FilePath<=2048 at construction) and instead tests a 512-char symbol completing normally; the OverLimitPacket reason kind is never asserted. Both reason kinds remain defined and constrained at the DB layer but are unexercised by tests.
findings.evidence: tasks.md T058: 'boundary rejection — missing Code Unit -> Failed with TerminalReasonKind.MissingCodeUnit'. tasks.md T059: 'boundary rejection — oversized packet -> Failed with TerminalReasonKind.OverLimitPacket'. SequentialScanRunnerFailureTests.cs T058 asserts Assert.ThrowsAsync<InvalidOperationException> and Phase==Pass1Planning (no Failed transition, no MissingCodeUnit). T059 asserts Phase==Completed with a 512-char symbol. CodeUnit.cs:65 enforces SymbolName<=512 and CodeUnit.cs:93 enforces FilePath<=2048 via RequireText, so the runner's ClassifyPacketRejection OverLimit branch (SequentialScanRunner.cs:296) is unreachable through the public API. The spec edge-case text says missing Code Unit 'refuses to start or, if detected mid-dispatch, fails the Scan' — throwing for an empty prepared set is a defensible 'refuses to start' reading, but the MissingCodeUnit reason kind is then dead code.
findings.remediation: Optional: either (a) add a unit test directly exercising ScanExecution.RecordBoundaryRejection with MissingCodeUnit and OverLimitPacket to cover the closed-enum contract, or (b) record MissingCodeUnit/OverLimitPacket as known-limitation reason kinds reserved for the Story 11.3 dispatcher path where the packet factory can be reached independently of CodeUnit. Not blocking for the expedited deadline slice.

findings.summary: FindActiveAsync uses OrderBy(e => e.StartedAt) on a DateTimeOffset property. AGENTS.md testing-discipline repo memory 'vulgata-test-harness' warns: 'avoid OrderBy on DateTimeOffset under SQLite (use FirstOrDefault/client-side ordering)'. The Story 11.1 ScanRunRepository uses the same pattern, so this is consistent with the existing codebase, but the warning stands.
findings.evidence: ScanExecutionRepository.cs:46-47: '.OrderBy(e => e.StartedAt).FirstOrDefaultAsync(cancellationToken)!;'. AGENTS.md: 'avoid OrderBy on DateTimeOffset under SQLite (use FirstOrDefault/client-side ordering)'.
findings.remediation: Optional: switch to FirstOrDefaultAsync without OrderBy (a Repository can only have one active Scan by design, so ordering is not load-bearing) or order client-side after FirstOrDefaultAsync. Not blocking — matches Story 11.1 pattern and the field is not load-bearing for the duplicate-detection contract.

findings.summary: PersistAsync does not implement the SQLite-safe parameterized no-op write-reservation pattern that plan.md §5 mandates ('For SQLite integration tests, the repository must not emit unsupported FOR UPDATE; it begins a serializable transaction and acquires the database-wide write reservation with a parameterized no-op update, mirroring the Story 11.1 pattern'). It only calls SaveChangesAsync inside a serializable transaction. KnowledgeStoreRepository.cs:63-66 implements the mandated pattern. This is a latent gap: no test exercises the real ScanExecutionRepository against SQLite (all G4 tests use in-memory fakes), so it does not currently fail, but the plan invariant is not honored.
findings.evidence: plan.md line 295-298: 'For SQLite integration tests, the repository must not emit unsupported FOR UPDATE; it begins a serializable transaction and acquires the database-wide write reservation with a parameterized no-op update, mirroring the Story 11.1 pattern.' ScanExecutionRepository.PersistAsync: 'await dbContext.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken); await transaction.CommitAsync(cancellationToken);' — no ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync no-op. Grep confirms no test references ScanExecutionRepository directly. The repository is also not registered in DI in Story 11.2 (deferred to Story 11.3 per workflow-state.last_checkpoint.plan_contradiction_resolved), so the gap is latent.
findings.remediation: When Story 11.3 registers ScanExecutionRepository and exercises it against SQLite, add the parameterized no-op UPDATE on the ScanExecutions row (or on Repositories like Story 11.1) inside the serializable transaction before mutation, mirroring KnowledgeStoreRepository.cs:63-66. Not blocking for Story 11.2 because the repository is unregistered and unexercised; record as a Story 11.3 precondition.

findings.summary: RecordingDispatcher is seeded with placeholder Valid envelopes whose JobId/ScanExecutionId do not match the dispatched packet (NonEmptyGuid(99)/NonEmptyGuid(88)). The runner's RunPass1Async does not verify identity match between the dispatched packet and the returned envelope — it uses result.Outcome only. The contract identity-match invariant (WorkerAgentResultEnvelope.Create validates JobId/ScanExecutionId/Kind match the dispatched packet) is therefore not exercised through the runner; it is only exercised by direct contract tests in SequentialScanRunnerContractTests. The GatedDispatcher and ConfigurableDispatcher do rewrite identity to match, so this is specific to the RecordingDispatcher path.
findings.evidence: SequentialScanRunnerDispatchTests.cs:598-606 CreateValidResultPlaceholder uses NonEmptyGuid(99)/NonEmptyGuid(88). SequentialScanRunner.cs:213-217 uses packet.JobId (local variable) for RecordValid, not result.JobId. WorkerAgentResultEnvelope contract requires the dispatcher to return a matching envelope; the fake honors it in GatedDispatcher.cs:149-153 and ConfigurableDispatcher.cs:88-96 but not in RecordingDispatcher.
findings.remediation: Optional: have RecordingDispatcher rewrite identity fields to match the dispatched packet (as GatedDispatcher and ConfigurableDispatcher already do) so the identity-match contract is honored uniformly. Not blocking — the runner does not assert identity match, so the placeholder envelopes do not cause false positives, and the contract is covered by direct contract tests.

findings.summary: IScanExecutionStore.ReadStateAsync XML doc claims it increments and persists the bounded restart indicator on a restart re-read, but the ScanExecutionRepository.ReadStateAsync implementation does NOT perform restart observation (it only maps to ScanExecutionStateView). The restart-observation logic lives in SequentialScanRunner.ReadStateAsync instead. The interface doc is stale/misleading relative to the implementation. The runner's ReadStateAsync is the authoritative path used by tests.
findings.evidence: IScanExecutionStore.cs:38-42: 'On a restart re-read of a Pass1Running row with a non-null InFlightJobId, the bounded restart indicator is incremented and persisted...'. ScanExecutionRepository.cs:69-94 ReadStateAsync: no ObserveRestart call, no PersistAsync. SequentialScanRunner.cs:99-135 ReadStateAsync: calls execution.ObserveRestart() and persists.
findings.remediation: Optional: correct the IScanExecutionStore.ReadStateAsync XML doc to reflect that it is a pure read mapping and that restart observation is owned by the runner, or remove the method from the port and let callers use GetAsync directly. Not blocking — the runner is the authoritative path and tests use it.

summary: Story 11.2 (Sequential Scan Runner & Typed Agent Dispatch) is ACCEPTED at candidate commit 9f1a6fb under the expedited-mvp execution level. All five acceptance criteria (AC-1 start/refusal, AC-2 sequential typed dispatch, AC-3 durable state across restart, AC-4 failure isolation, AC-5 deterministic completion) are implemented and met by the production code; FR-001..FR-015 are satisfied with no out-of-scope behavior introduced (no public API, UI, Chat tool, Scan parsing, Pass 2, Cross-Repository Resolution, retry, failover, or Story 11.3 document generation). The typed Worker Agent job packet and result envelope are closed allowlists with finite UTF-8/count limits and the Story 11.1 KnowledgeTextSafety.EnsureSafe guard applied to every string; absolute host paths, parent traversal, secrets, private keys, stack traces, and oversized content are rejected before dispatch. The additive migration 20260801033655_AddSequentialScanRunner is additive only, uses Restrict/NoAction FKs, has the three closed-enum/bound CHECK constraints, alternate keys, and indexes, rolls back cleanly to the Story 11.1 baseline 20260731041654_AddMinimalKnowledgeStore, and has-pending-model-changes exits 0. Verification: dotnet build => 0 errors; dotnet test --filter SequentialScanRunner => 62 passed, 0 failed; full non-final-image regression => 744 passed, 0 failed. TDD discipline is evidenced by the commit chain (G1 contracts 8631f73 -> G2 start 51927db -> G3 dispatch+completion daf5314 -> G4 restart 7df4a35 -> G5 failure 5692af4 -> G6 migration b4f34df -> Polish 3e299e1/195aedf). The documented plan-contradiction resolution (T073 deferred SequentialScanRunner DI registration to Story 11.3 because IWorkerAgentDispatcher has no production implementation in Story 11.2, per plan.md line 191) is correct, consistent with the plan's scoping, and truthfully recorded in workflow-state.json.last_checkpoint.plan_contradiction_resolved; only the three Infrastructure adapters were registered in Program.cs with an explanatory comment. Story 11.1 invariants are not weakened — the runner holds no IKnowledgeStoreRepository reference and commits no Document Version. Architecture seams are clean: Core has no EF/infra deps, Infrastructure owns EF/migration/configuration, Web only registers DI. Ubiquitous language matches verbatim (Scan, Repository, Code Unit, Worker Agent, Pre-Scan, Pass 1, Cross-Repository). Five low-severity findings are recorded (F001-F005): two test-coverage gaps for the MissingCodeUnit/OverLimitPacket reason kinds (structurally unreachable via the public CodeUnit API but unexercised), the PersistAsync SQLite-safe no-op pattern not mirroring the plan's Story 11.1 invariant (latent because the repository is unregistered and unexercised), a stale IScanExecutionStore.ReadStateAsync XML doc, an OrderBy-on-DateTimeOffset pattern matching the existing codebase but flagged by the test-harness memory, and placeholder-envelope identity mismatch in the RecordingDispatcher. None are blocking: the expedited deadline scope is met, all deferred items (concurrency, leases, replay, failover, retry, Pass 2, Cross-Repository Resolution, LLM Worker Agent, SequentialScanRunner DI registration) are truthfully recorded as limitations rather than claimed complete, and no failing test is committed.
